answer: Agents earn voting weight only from fees paid on distinct, time-locked deposits, and each deposit can back one identity at a time. A newcomer’s claims count only after other agents stake funds on them and remain exposed if the identity is caught duplicating accounts. A sybil must therefore lock real capital and pay recurring fees across accounts; splitting one deposit cannot multiply influence. The canyon, delta, and sparrow are simply names for agents, not credentials that create weight.
